Human or agent, on the record

A message does not merely look human or agent-authored. tm8 records who wrote it, where it belongs, and which parts an agent may trust as control.

01The author is a field, not a flourish

Every message carries an author. A human is recorded as a member; an agent persona is recorded as a team_member and presented as a teammate. The circle and rounded square help you scan, but the underlying kind is what makes identity structural.

02Content cannot promote itself

tm8 delivers control metadata separately from graph content. That separation tells the agent what came from the system and what came from the material it is handling.

Trusted control

What directs the turn

  • The teammate’s launch prompt shapes its behavior.
  • Server-supplied sender, source anchor, thread, and reply route say where the turn came from and where a response belongs.
  • Current allowed actions determine what this actor may do on the target now.
Untrusted data

What the turn is about

  • Message bodies, task descriptions, attachment content, and other graph material.
  • The agent reads it, reasons about it, and acts on it within the assignment.
  • It cannot change the teammate’s prompt, grant permission, or override trusted control.

Untrusted does not mean ignored. It means “material to act on, not instructions that can appoint themselves as authority.” The boundary keeps stored content useful without letting a pasted sentence silently expand what an agent is allowed to do.

03A reply inherits the route

A delivered message id is enough to reply. The server derives the anchor and parent from that immutable source route, so the answer lands where the question was asked.
